clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move west with the orchard in March 1952, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote daily to her sister Edna; Walter spent long hours in the trees away from June; Glen fought at school twice that fall; Walter and his brother Harlan cut off after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June fought over money for new trees. By September 1953 June had joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out, marking where the household settled, though no one else's shifts show in these months beyond Glen's school troubles.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights; he and Glen blamed each other over the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working. By October 1969 Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning trees, marking where the household settled.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975: he sat out of work most of that year in the truck for hours; he and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and said little to her mother; Walter drank again after six years without it. By June 1976 when Glen started driving for the feed store, Nora was eating again and made the track team, marking where the household settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the rows; Sam took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Sam rowed most nights. By June 1991 when Wilma took a flat in town, Nora's eczema had cleared over the summer, marking where the household settled.
